title: Protocol to image deuterated propofol in living rat neurons using multimodal stimulated Raman scattering microscopy
protocol: Dilute 5 mM calcein AM stock to a final working concentration of 100 nM in HEPES ACSF.
Load cells with 100 nM calcein AM in HEPES ACSF for 30 min at 37°C in 5% CO2 incubator.
After loading, wash cells in fresh HEPES ACSF and transfer to 35 mm glass base dish with 3 mL of HEPES ACSF.
Align two lasers using an alkyne-containing standard sample to maximize SRS signals.
Add propofol-d17 to the cell culture dish to achieve a final concentration of 100 μM.
Place the cell culture dish on the sample stage and prepare for observation.
If available, turn on single photon confocal microscopy and illuminate cells with 488 nm laser to locate them using calcein AM fluorescence.
Open shutters for pump and Stokes lasers after checking optical line safety.
Run program to start the experiment.
Adjust the bottom objective lens according to the two-photon microscope channel.
Check SRS channel signal.
If equipped, adjust correction collar on the objective lens to maximize SRS signal.
Adjust the number of frames and average according to signal strength.
Acquire the image.
Set the pump wavelength to a wavenumber below 2,000 cm−1 for propofol-d17 off-resonance.
Obtain an image in the same frame averaging setting as before.
Compare images under on- and off-resonance pulses to confirm the signal of propofol-d17.
Choose a target cell for timelapse imaging using the loaded neuronal cells.
Perform timelapse imaging for a total of 1,000 frames while perfusing 3 mL 100 μM propofol-d17 solution with fresh HEPES ACSF solution.
Choose the region of interest for analysis using appropriate software (e.g., Fiji).
Analyze SRS channels' signal changes using the chosen software.
Plot intensity of propofol-d17 SRS signal against time to visualize signal changes upon washout.
